scope: Corollary 6.1 (Non-neighbors and directed cycles) of the manuscript “A proof of Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture” (preprints/A-proof-of-Seymours-second-neighborhood-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 173 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 20be859799f83e34), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 13-14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D be a nonempty finite oriented graph of order n. For v ∈ V (D), write N− 1 (v) = {u : u → v}, d± (v) = |N± 1 (v)|, δ± (D) = min x∈V (D) d± (x). Define the non-neighbors of v, excluding v itself, by Z(v) = V (D) \ ( {v} ∪ N+ 1 (v) ∪ N− 1 (v) ) . Then the following hold. (i) If D has no directed 3-cycle, then some vertex v satisfies d+ (v) ≤ |Z(v)|, n − 1 ≥ 2d+ (v) + d− (v). (ii) If δ+(D) ≥ n/3 and δ−(D) ≥ n/3, then D contains a directed 3-cycle. 13 (iii) If r ≥ 1 is an integer, d+(v) = d−(v) = r for every vertex, and D has directed girth exactly four, then n ≥ 3r + 1. Here directed girth is the length of a shortest directed cycle.
